comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 135 hash-matched manifest entries: 130 BDDL definitions, three benchmark-registry files, and two predicate files. Searched the complete inventory for adjustment, turning, locking, fastener, tool, and articulated-mechanism tasks; then read the closest BDDL definition and its TurnOn predicate implementation completely.
comparisons.objective: The candidate sets a gripper opening stop to 90°, locks that adjustable setting with a jam nut, releases the tools, and verifies retention through repeated articulation. LIBERO's closest objective merely turns on a stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, coupled countertorque, regrasping, withdrawal, and lever cycling. LIBERO: single-fixture stove activation; the supplied backend delegates to arg.turn_on() and specifies no second tool, locknut, counterholding, or retained adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate success requires angular tolerance, nut seating and retention, three repeatable cycles, limited drift, and hands-off clearance. The LIBERO goal is the binary Turnon predicate.

closest_tasks.name: Turn on the stove
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Manipulate a stove control sufficiently for its turn_on state to become true.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares rotary control manipulation only; it does not preserve an adjustable screw against jam-nut reaction or test retained motion after locking.

comparisons.reason: The complete supplied LIBERO registry contains no task whose tested outcome combines precise stop adjustment, concentric two-tool locking, and released cyclic retention.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 381 hash-matched manifest entries: 379 kitchen task implementations plus the environment and dataset registries. Searched every inventoried path and source for adjustment, rotation, knobs, screws, nuts, locking, tools, and fasteners; read the closest registered atomic implementation completely.
comparisons.objective: The candidate establishes and mechanically locks an opening limit, then function-tests it. RoboCasa's closest task changes a toaster-oven temperature control relative to its initial setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: bimanual driver/wrench counterholding on coupled screw-and-nut hardware followed by articulated verification. RoboCasa: manipulate one appliance temperature control in the requested direction.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate: within 3° of 90°, nuts retained, three returns within tolerance, drift at most 2°, and released clearance. RoboCasa: temperature state changes by at least 0.15 in the requested direction.

closest_tasks.name: AdjustToasterOvenTemperature
closest_tasks.objective: Increase or decrease toaster-oven temperature from a randomized initial state.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Operate a single appliance adjustment control.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The normalized temperature changes at least 0.15 in the commanded direction.
closest_tasks.reason: Both involve adjustment, but RoboCasa neither locks the setting under reaction torque nor verifies hands-off retention through repeated mechanism cycles.

comparisons.reason: No inventoried RoboCasa task tests coupled screw adjustment plus jam-nut counterholding and post-lock functional retention.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 11 hash-matched selected source files and checked the complete 25-name ENVIRONMENTS registry and its environment mappings. Searched all implementations for rotational adjustment, fasteners, locks, tools, and articulated controls; read the closest drawer implementation completely.
comparisons.objective: The candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop before repeated verification. SimplerEnv's nearest articulated task opens a selected cabinet drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: precise two-tool rotational force coordination and functional cycling. SimplerEnv: grasp or push a drawer and translate its prismatic joint.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate uses angle, nut retention, repeated return, drift, and released-clearance requirements. OpenDrawer succeeds once drawer qpos is at least 0.15.

closest_tasks.name: google_robot_open_drawer / OpenDrawerCustomInScene-v0
closest_tasks.success_condition: Drawer joint position reaches at least 0.15.
closest_tasks.reason: It exercises an articulated mechanism but has no calibrated angular setting, fastener locking, countertorque, or repeated retention test.

comparisons.reason: The complete SimplerEnv registry is limited to pick, place, move-near, stacking, and drawer tasks and contains no matching lock-and-retain ability.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 1,122 hash-matched manifest entries: 1,018 current BDDL activity definitions, 101 legacy definitions, and three OmniGibson predicate/task backends. Searched the complete activity inventory for assembly, installation, repair, adjustment, locking, screws, and fasteners; read assembling_furniture and the full AttachedTo backend in bounded chunks.
comparisons.objective: The candidate adjusts and locks an already-assembled industrial gripper stop and then verifies retained motion. BEHAVIOR's closest assembly task attaches a desk bracket to a top and four legs to the bracket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: coaxial tooling, bimanual countertorque, angular regulation, and cyclic verification. BEHAVIOR: align attachment meta-links; the backend then forms a fixed or spherical joint.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires numeric angle accuracy, nut seating/retention, repeated returns, drift control, and tool clearance. BEHAVIOR requires Attached predicates for the bracket, top, and all legs.

closest_tasks.name: assembling_furniture-0
closest_tasks.objective: Assemble a desk top, bracket, and four legs.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bring compatible male and female attachment links into positional and angular alignment.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The bracket is attached to the top and every leg is attached to the bracket.
closest_tasks.reason: Backend inspection resolves Attached as proximity/alignment followed by joint creation, not physical screw adjustment, jam-nut counterholding, or retained-angle testing.

comparisons.reason: Even the closest BEHAVIOR assembly predicate measures completed component attachment rather than preservation and verification of a mechanically locked adjustment.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both official JSON files against their manifest hashes and checked all ten published Tier-1 setup records against the task_catalog IDs; also examined the linked procedure records while excluding explicitly unselected drafts from benchmark coverage. The closest published tasks are DC-knob and DC-key.
comparisons.objective: The candidate sets a precise gripper stop, mechanically locks it, and verifies repeated retained travel. DC-knob turns a dimmer to a mark; DC-key turns and releases a two-position key.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: coordinated driver and wrench use under coupled reaction torque, followed by tool withdrawal and lever cycling. DataCenterBench: single-control rotation, with release required only for DC-key.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate combines tolerance, two-nut retention, three cycles, drift limit, and clearance dwell. DC-knob checks pointer position; DC-key checks the alternate position and gripper release.

closest_tasks.name: DC-knob — Turn the knob to the mark
closest_tasks.quote: Turn the round knob on the white box clockwise until the black line on it points at the black mark on the box.
closest_tasks.objective: Rotate a fixed rotary dimmer from its start mark to its goal mark.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full score when the knob line points at the goal mark; partial credit for noticeable clockwise progress.
closest_tasks.reason: It shares target-angle control, but not a threaded stop, separate locking nut, counterholding, or cyclic proof that the setting remained locked.

closest_tasks.name: DC-key — Turn the key
closest_tasks.quote: Turn the key clockwise to its other position. Leave it there and release it.
closest_tasks.objective: Move a key switch to its alternate detented position and release it.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Rotate and release a single retained control.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Full score when the key reaches the other position and the gripper releases it.
closest_tasks.reason: Hands-off state retention is shared, but the detented key has no adjustable screw/nut coupling, precision lock operation, or repeated mechanism verification.

comparisons.reason: The closest published controls cover target rotation or released retention separately; neither tests locking an adjustable stop against reaction torque and proving retention over cycles.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 110 hash-matched manifest entries covering the dynamic task loader, 54 task implementations, and 55 YAML configurations. Searched the complete Python/YAML inventory for screws, nuts, tightening, locking, tools, adjustment, and rotation; read fasten_screws.py and its configuration completely.
comparisons.objective: The candidate tunes one adjustment screw, locks it with a jam nut without changing the setting, and verifies retained gripper motion. RoboDojo fasten_screws inserts and tightens three color-matched screws/nuts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate: coaxial driver seating plus simultaneous wrench counterholding on a coupled adjustment. RoboDojo: repeated fastener insertion/tightening and color matching; its scorer observes alignment and insertion depth rather than torque or lock preservation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires target angle, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, bounded drift, and released clearance. RoboDojo awards transitions for one, two, or three upright, coaxial, sufficiently inserted fastener pairs with grippers open.

closest_tasks.name: fasten_screws
closest_tasks.quote: Insert and tighten each screw into the nut of the same color.
closest_tasks.objective: Insert and tighten three screws into matching nuts.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Coaxially align and insert multiple fastener pairs, then open the grippers.
closest_tasks.success_condition: Each credited pair is upright, within 1 mm in XY, and inserted to the configured depth; higher scores require more completed pairs.
closest_tasks.reason: This is the strongest primitive overlap, but its observable outcome is fastener insertion depth, not preserving a calibrated setting during jam-nut locking and verifying cycle retention.

comparisons.reason: RoboDojo covers generic screw/nut fastening, but the candidate's central tested ability—counterholding a calibrated adjustment through locknut reaction and validating retained function—is absent.
